title: AI Doesn't Read Words. Here's What It Reads Instead
description: AI models don't read words like you do. They read tokens. Here's what tokens are, how a model uses them, and why it explains some strange AI mistakes. Follow for a new AI lesson every day. #shorts #ai #learnai #claude #tokens

scenes.narration: AI doesn't read words like you do. It reads something smaller.
It reads tokens. A token is a small chunk of text. Often a whole word, sometimes just part of one.

visual.title: *Tokens*
visual.subtitle: Small chunks of text: a word, or part of one

scenes.narration: Here's what happens. Your message is split into tokens. Each token becomes a number. Then the model predicts the most likely next token, again and again.
That's why AI can stumble on tasks like counting letters in a word. It sees chunks, not single letters.

visual.title: Why letters *trip* it up
items: AI sees: a few token chunks

scenes.narration: Try it yourself. Ask Claude to explain tokens like you're ten.

visual.title: Try this prompt
items: Imagine cutting a sentence into puzzle pieces. Each piece is a token, and I read them one by one.
